subject: Private CP: IDP fanout, SCIM delta cleanup, and emergency role fallback plan
messages:
From: Katie Wang <katie@nimblehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.company>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>
Date: 2025-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial config export for SCIM / SAML sync

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the quick export. We pulled the SCIM delta you sent and found ~420 entries flagged as 'conflict: duplicateAttribute' (email vs employeeId). Our identity team is asking whether Redwood's private control plane will support fanout assertions for operator nodes in our VPC (we run three operator subnets separated by AZ).

Two quick asks from our side before we start a merge attempt:
- Can Redwood fanout the SAML assertion to multiple operator endpoints while preserving the original NameID and a stable role claim?
- Do you have a recommended dedupe strategy for the SCIM patch you provided (we prefer to keep employeeId authoritative, but emails are used downstream in internal apps)?

If we can get a short runbook for the emergency fallback role (operator-admin emergency access) and the exact claim name you emit for role mapping, we can test in our staging VPC tomorrow.

— Katie
Identity Engineer, Nimble Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.company>
To: Katie Wang <katie@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.company>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.company>
Date: 2025-06-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial config export for SCIM / SAML sync

Thanks Katie — good questions. Quick summary of what Redwood supports and what I think will work for Nimble: 

1) SAML fanout: our Private Control Plane (private-controlplane agent) supports assertion fanout to multiple operator endpoints behind the VPC NAT/ALB. We preserve NameID and emit a stable claim called "redwood_role" and a supplemental "redwood_operator_id" claim when operator routing is in use. The mapping table is attached (saml-assertion-mapping-v2.yaml).

2) SCIM dedupe: we recommend authoritative employeeId as you suggested. We include a two-pass patch: first a dry-run to mark duplicates in SCIM (attached CSV) and second an attribute-merge that writes canonical email to "workEmail" and moves older emails into "previousEmails". We will run the dry-run with you.

3) Emergency fallback: short plan below and full runbook attached: 
- Emergency role: redwood:operator:emergency (time-limited, audit-only privileged token).
- Activation path: HubSpot pipeline + exec approval + ephemeral token issuance via console with JIT logging.
- Revocation: automatic 8-hour TTL + forced rekey on next normal roll.

Next steps I propose: staged cutover in your staging VPC this week: Tuesday 6/30 10:00-13:00 PT for fanout smoke, Wed 7/1 09:00-11:00 PT for SCIM dry-run, Thu 7/2 14:00-16:00 PT for role-fallback drill. Ben, can you own ops runway? Laura, can you confirm runbook link/retention on logs? Dev, can you validate the YAML mapping for edge cases?

Thanks — Monica
Head of Field Integrations, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.company>, Katie Wang <katie@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.company>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.company>
Date: 2025-06-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP: IDP fanout, SCIM delta cleanup, and emergency role fallback plan

On Tue, Jun 30, 2025 at 09:03 AM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.company> wrote:
> Next steps I propose: staged cutover in your staging VPC this week ...

We're good to own the ops runway. Quick notes from the infra side after the fanout smoke this morning: 
- Fanout worked to operator-A and operator-B behind the ALB, but operator-C returned 502s due to a misconfigured private route (Nimble's side). We captured a full trace (attached).
- Assertion size increased due to "previousEmails" attribute; ALB body size is fine but we recommend a 64KB assertion cap in your IDP settings to avoid SAML truncation in edge proxies.
- For the SCIM dry-run, please push the delta CSV into the test SCIM endpoint we provided (scim-staging.nimble.local) with the header X-Redwood-DryRun: true.

I'll be on the call Tue 10:00 PT to review traces if you want.

— Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Katie Wang <katie@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.company>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.company>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.company>
Date: 2025-07-01T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP: IDP fanout, SCIM delta cleanup, and emergency role fallback plan

Thanks Ben — that trace was super helpful. Follow-ups from our side after the dry-run this morning: 
- We patched the private route and operator-C now accepts assertions. Fanout validated across all three operator subnets.
- We set a 48KB assertion cap on the IDP temporarily to see behavior; no truncation seen yet. We'll revert once you move the "previousEmails" into a compressed JSON blob on your side.
- SCIM dry-run flagged 18 accounts with legacy MFA bindings tied to old email addresses. We need to decide whether to rebind MFA automatically or surface as a ticket to our internal ITSM.

For the emergency fallback drill on Thu 7/2 at 14:00 PT — we will schedule our security lead (Amit Kumar) to approve activation and observe logs. Please send the exact play-by-play you'll follow for activation and revocation.

— Katie

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.company>
To: Katie Wang <katie@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.company>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.company>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.company>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.company>
Date: 2025-07-02T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private CP: IDP fanout, SCIM delta cleanup, and emergency role fallback plan

Great alignment — appreciate you pulling Amit into the drill. Final checklist and play-by-play for Thursday drill (attached in runbook): 

1) Pre-checks (13:30 PT): verify staging ALB health for operator-{A,B,C}, ensure SCIM staging endpoint responsive, collect baseline audit tokens.
2) Activation (14:00 PT): Nimble security lead submits HubSpot approval form -> Monica triggers ephemeral redwood:operator:emergency token issuance (console) -> Token bound to operator-id and marked TTL=8h.
3) Observability (14:05 PT): Ben watches trace pipeline and X-Request-Id correlation; Laura verifies audit log retention flags in Control Plane console.
4) Revocation (14:30 PT): Monica revokes token via console, automatic TTL should also expire at 14:00 next day if not revoked. Confirm revocation with an immediate probe to operator endpoints.
4a) Postmortem (15:00 PT): collect evidence (audit log export) and create postmortem doc in shared drive.

Open items we still need to close: 
- Dev to update saml-assertion-mapping-v2.yaml to compress historical email list into a base64 blob to keep assertion sizes below 48KB.
- Laura to confirm log retention window for emergency activations (we recommend 365 days for customers with compliance needs).
- Katie to confirm whether Nimble wants automatic rebind of MFA during SCIM patch or to surface tickets.

If that looks good I'll push the updated YAML and the cutover runbook to the shared folder and we can run the drill. Thanks everyone.

— Monica
Head of Field Integrations, Redwood Inference
